simple.meaning: בָּקַשׁ (bâqash) is a Hebrew action word meaning “to search out (by any method, specifically in worship or prayer); by implication, to strive after.” BibleIQ anchors the English reading to this source verb before comparing its uses.
simple.biblicalBackground: This action appears 225 times in Genesis, Exodus, Leviticus, Numbers, Deuteronomy, and 12 more, beginning at Genesis 31:39. The surrounding contexts include family, flock, kingship, land.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to בָּקַשׁ (H1245) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Actions in Scripture show what people do, what God does, and how covenant faithfulness or rebellion is described. BibleIQ compares the action across its occurrences.
simple.summary: בָּקַשׁ (bâqash) / H1245 is traced through Genesis 31:39, Genesis 37:15, Genesis 37:16, Genesis 43:9 with source-language evidence and verse context.
